channel.description: Latest articles from Public Health Post (publichealthpost.org)

item.title: The Unequal Health Legacy of the 2008 Recession
item.description: A recent study reveals that economic crises magnify inequalities already deeply embedded in political and financial systems.

item.title: When Floods Turn Toxic
item.description: When Hurricane Harvey hit in 2017, people of color were more exposed to toxic floodwaters and were left with deeper worries for the future.

item.title: Redefining Disability with Inclusive Sports
item.description: Organized sports are one way for adults with disabilities to maintain regular exercise while also building social connections.

item.title: Teen Sleep Loss Is a Public Health Problem, Not Just a Phase
item.description: The mismatch between adolescents' internal sleep regulation and external expectations reflects a structural problem, not personal failings.

item.title: When Health Advice Comes With No Waiting Room
item.description: Chatbots can provide clear advice for routine health questions, but their accuracy declines substantially for more urgent scenarios.

item.title: Black Mothers, Broken System: The Maternal Mortality Gap
item.description: Structural forces like bias, unequal access to resources, and cumulative stress interact to shape pregnancy outcomes for Black women.

item.title: Shifting the Costs of Nursing Home Care
item.description: Cuts under the OBBBA could push states and nursing homes to revive filial laws, forcing adult children to pay for parents’ long-term care.

item.title: Rethinking Consciousness: A Conversation with Dr. Joseph Giacino
item.description: Joseph Giacino, director of the Disorders of Consciousness Program at Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital, shares how updated guidelines may reshape care for those with severe brain injury.

item.title: Deconstructing the Opioid Crisis
item.description: OxyContin serves as a powerful example of how corporate interest can drastically shape medical practice and health worldwide.

item.title: The Sound of Survival, and the Silence of Survivorship
item.description: The end of childhood cancer treatment marks the beginning of a lifetime of care and health challenges that largely go unacknowledged.
